title: Pager aftercare playbook & quick todo
content:
Context: page landed at 02:18 UTC — alerts showed sustained elevated 5xx rate from hosted inference frontdoor for ~3m, spike correlated with batched-generation jobs from a single customer (dedicated burst policy).

Immediate summary (what I did):
- 02:18 — woke, skimmed /alerts and /dashboards (latency p50/p95 rising, p99 and 5xx spikes).
- 02:19 — Slack incident channel: #ops-pager; posted initial note + asked for traffic dump from frontdoor-proxy (requested by Evan).
- 02:21 — Identified repeated KV cache misses on predictor-3 (kv shard 4) causing backpressure; CPU on predictor pod ~98%.
- 02:25 — Rolled traffic to fallback model variant (predictor-3-small) using routing policy to protect latency-critical teams.
- 02:32 — Began controlled restart of 3/5 predictor-3 replicas (staggered) — observed steady recovery of latency and dropping 5xx.
- 02:45 — Put mitigation in place (short-term): temporary routing rule + scale-up prediction workers by 2 nodes for burst window.
- 03:05 — Alert cleared; continued monitoring until 04:00. No customer-visible data loss reported.

Root-cause hypothesis:
- Sequence: unusually large batched requests from a single customer -> KV cache churn + eviction storm on kv shard 4 -> predictor-3 worker threads overloaded -> internal queue growth -> 5xx on the frontdoor when internal timeouts reached.
- Contributing: predictor-3 model config has small kv-cache headroom under high concurrency; autoscaler did not trigger fast enough because burst was short and CPU reclaim was delayed by garbage collection.

Immediate follow-ups (owners + rough ETA):
- A1: Add a short-term autoscaler override for predictor-3 to respond to p95 CPU > 80% faster (temp policy). Owner: Evan Li. ETA: 2026-07-23.
- A2: Instrument kv-cache eviction rate per shard in telemetry (new metric). Owner: Asha Menon. ETA: 2026-07-25.
- A3: Post-incident customer outreach: coordinate with CS to notify affected account, include mitigation and next steps. Owner: Priya Singh (CS). ETA: 2026-07-22.
- A4: Create a gating rule in smart-routing to detect short, high-concurrency batch floods and apply token-mux rate-limiter or fallback earlier. Owner: Infra team (PR queued). ETA: 2026-08-02.
- A5: Runbook gap: existing predictor runbook lacks explicit kv-shard eviction troubleshooting steps. Add a section and sample commands. Owner: Asha Menon + SRE docs. ETA: 2026-07-28.

Runbook TODO (concrete items to add):
- Quick checks: `kubectl top pod -n infra predictor-3` (filter by kv-shard labels), `curl` endpoints for /metrics?shard=4 to see eviction_rate, `redis-cli info` on local cache store.
- Safe mitigation steps: how to perform staggered rolling restart of predictor-3 replicas without dropping the KV cache for other shards (script snippet + recommended wait times).
- Autoscaler tuning recipe: recommended thresholds for short bursts (<5m) vs sustained load, and how to temporary override with `infractl autoscaler set --policy burst-rapid`.
- How to detect a single-customer flood: queries to request logs: `select count(*) by customer_id where batch_size > 64 and timestamp > now() - 10m` and example alert rule to create.

Notes & oddities observed (for postmortem):
- GC spikes on predictor-3 JVM at 02:20 coincident with peak CPU. Heap growth pattern looks like large ephemeral allocations from batch pre-processing.
- One predictor-3 pod was on node with older NVIDIA driver (minor mismatch) — scheduling placed it there because of binpacking; need to verify driver compatibility doesn't degrade perf.
- Predictors 1/2 unaffected — skewed by shard placement. We should consider shard rebalancing heuristics.

Quick commands I used (repo: infra):
- `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/predictor-3 --timeout=10m` (stagger via delay script)
- `infractl routing set --route predictor-3 -> predictor-3-small --temporarily 30m` to move traffic off the heavy variant
- `promql: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)` to compare eviction hot spots

Post-incident checklist (what must be done before we close the loop):
- [ ] Add eviction metric and dashboard tile (Asha)
- [ ] Draft runbook section + include staggered restart snippet (Asha)
- [ ] Autoscaler override PR + testing on staging (Evan)
- [ ] Customer comms drafted and approved (Priya)
- [ ] Driver/version compatibility audit for predictor nodes (Infra)
- [ ] Follow-up incident review scheduled (30–60 min) and postmortem write-up (owner: Asha; target date 2026-07-27)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we increase default kv-cache headroom for predictor-3 family? Tradeoff: memory cost vs fewer eviction storms. Proposal: +25% headroom for predictor-3 only, evaluate over 2 weeks.
- Is the short-burst autoscaler option acceptable company-wide? Might increase costs; need product/finance signoff.

Notes to self: keep the postmortem short (one page), include timeline + clear action owners. Attach telemetry graphs (p50/p95/p99, eviction rate, pod CPU). Link PR and Jira in the write-up.

End of run — left notes in #ops-pager and tagged Priya/Evan. Will follow up tomorrow with a short review at 11:00 PT if everyone can make it.

-- Asha
